# plugin-hostd / fuzz_reply

plugin-hostd's own fuzz target `fuzz_reply` ([source](source/fuzz_reply.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over plugin-hostd 0.10.0 (FreeMixer/plugin-hostd at 65cd2b02).

Opens one worker feedback source in plugin-hostd's relay, src/relay.c, then reads the input as up to 512 operations: add a source (at most four), have a source write bytes, read a source, close or remove a source, remove an instance, interrupt a receive, send an event of the daemon's own, limit or interrupt the controller's sends, or make the controller go away. Its own recv and send stand in for the sockets, so no socket or thread is used. A reference splitter follows what each source wrote. At the end the relay is shut down.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- No library is linked: the harness includes src/relay.c of plugin-hostd 0.10.0 at commit 65cd2b02 in its own source, with recv, send, shutdown, close and fcntl renamed to the harness's own and a line limit of 6000 bytes, as plugin-hostd's Makefile builds it, but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- After every operation each source's buffer holds at most 6000 bytes of an unfinished line, never more than its capacity, and its capacity stays under 20192 bytes ([lines 337-355](source/fuzz_reply.c#L337-L355)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each read, and when a source or an instance is removed, the controller reads every complete line the source wrote that is 6000 bytes or shorter, once each, unchanged and in order; while the controller is gone nothing reaches it ([lines 403-432](source/fuzz_reply.c#L403-L432)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After a read, and when a source or an instance is removed, the relay has taken every byte the worker wrote to each source it still reads ([lines 434-445](source/fuzz_reply.c#L434-L445)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- When a source goes, or an instance, or the relay shuts down, the relay writes one "param_gesture <instance> <symbol> end" line for each gesture that source's lines began and did not end (for an instance, only its own), and no other line ([lines 454-493](source/fuzz_reply.c#L454-L493)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An event of the daemon's own reaches the controller as one line, exactly as written, and after each operation the controller has read no line the reference does not account for ([lines 495-527](source/fuzz_reply.c#L495-L527)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- What the controller reads in each operation ends on a whole line: no line is cut short ([lines 357-374](source/fuzz_reply.c#L357-L374)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The relay sends only on the controller's socket, never on a worker's ([lines 278-285](source/fuzz_reply.c#L278-L285)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The relay follows each new worker socket it is handed ([lines 587-591](source/fuzz_reply.c#L587-L591)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
